newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls to 13.0/14.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls to 13.0/14.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 13.0/14.0 percent from 17.0 percent on Friday morning on the back of relatively ample liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said liquidity was not as tight as initially feared, causing overnight money and short-dated swap rates to fall.
One foreign bank dealer said central bank injection of 779 billion rupiah helped ease supply and calmed operators despite worries over the month-end factor and weekly tax payments.
However, one Japanese bank dealer said operators should remain cautious because the condition could change in the afternoon on the month-end factor.
"I think tax payments due today are relatively high. I just worry that overnight money may rise again," he said.
The dealer said one-week money had stabilised to around 14.0 percent from 15.0 percent on Thursday.
Overnight swap was last at 1.25/2.00 points, compared with a high of tom/next swap on Thursday at 3.75 points. Tom/next swap had fallen to 0.5/0.6 points from 1.0 at the opening.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 9.75 percent, compared with 8.32 percent on Wednesday.
